title: WMI Event Filter (Sysmon Alert)
rationale: Requires nonempty/non-dash RuleName. Current Sysmon profile has no named WMI predicates; WMI registration also needs attribution by owned object identity beyond the existing process-GUID join. No automatic admission merely because Event 19 is collected.

title: Proc Exec (Non-Exe Filetype)
rationale: Hayabusa-native rather than Sigma-derived. Executing a benign non-.exe helper is plausible but duplicates image-name mechanism and changes the stated rule-origin scope; not a priority.

title: WMI Event Consumer (Sysmon Alert)
rationale: Same RuleName dependency and WMI object-attribution gap for Event 20. A collector-generated named match is a different experimental profile.

title: WMI Event Consumer To Filter (Sysmon Alert)
rationale: Same RuleName dependency and WMI attribution gap for Event 21. Binding introduces activation/lifecycle complexity; defer.

title: Clipboard Change (Sysmon Alert)
rationale: Hayabusa-native Event 24 plus nonempty/non-dash RuleName. Requires collector-profile and session/clipboard fixture work; not a simple additional test under present profile.

title: Proc Tampering
rationale: Event 25 requires a real image-tampering mechanism, not ordinary process creation. Adds substantial mechanism and attribution complexity and is Hayabusa-native; defer from this bounded runtime comparison.

title: Raw Access Read
rationale: Hayabusa-native event-only rule can incidentally match the proposed Sigma raw-read case. Do not count it as a second independent case or silently change the Sigma-only primary selection.

title: Rare Remote Thread Creation By Uncommon Source Image
rationale: Requires one of many named source applications. A renamed probe is not evidence of those applications behavior; common-tool execution would dominate. Existing remote-thread case is a better controlled basis.

title: Remote Thread Creation By Uncommon Source Image
rationale: Requires explorer/msiexec/other named application identity and complex exclusions. Not a simple language-native port under current fixture contract.

title: Creation Of a Suspicious ADS File Outside a Browser Download
rationale: Alternative to numeric-IP Contents regex: requires the exact flattened ZoneTransfer/ZoneId prefix and executable-like filename, excluding browsers. Qualify actual Sysmon formatting first; avoid counting both content rules as separate mechanisms.

title: Suspicious File Download From File Sharing Websites -  File Stream
rationale: Contents domain list plus stream-extension predicate. Reuses the same proposed ADS operation with another string; record incidental matches instead of making a separate experiment solely to raise counts.

title: Unusual File Download from Direct IP Address
rationale: Adds Event 15 Contents regex to the existing stream-hash case. Write fixed synthetic Zone.Identifier text with a numeric-IP URL to an owned matching-extension carrier; verify bytes. This tests stream-content evidence, not a real download. Confirm live Contents formatting and process attribution.

title: Backup Files Deleted
rationale: Requires deletion by listed cmd/PowerShell/rundll32-like image. Deleting an owned .bak file with the native program would not match; a shell wrapper adds little runtime discrimination.

title: Potentially Suspicious Self Extraction Directive File Created
rationale: Same Event 29 profile gap with a .sed filename predicate. Incremental indicator coverage only; no separate mechanism.

title: CredUI.DLL Loaded By Uncommon Process
rationale: Alternative genuine system-DLL load from a nonexcluded program path. No credential UI or credential access is needed to test the load predicate. Shares the proposed signed-DLL mechanism; choose one primary target.

title: Load Of RstrtMgr.DLL By An Uncommon Process
rationale: Adds legitimate signed OS-library loading to the existing unsigned .node fixture. Load the genuine fixed RstrtMgr.dll from its system path without invoking Restart Manager operations. Freeze DLL hash and measured executable path outside exclusions; verify module identity. Reject if it is already loaded in controls or the control emits the selected alert.

title: Potential System DLL Sideloading From Non System Locations
rationale: A stock-listed DLL basename outside approved locations can match. Loading a renamed harmless fixture would mostly duplicate existing unsigned .node loading plus a path/name predicate; it would not prove actual search-order hijacking.

title: Potential Vcruntime140 DLL Sideloading
rationale: Legitimate validly signed C Runtime Library metadata is explicitly filtered. Ordinary CRT startup is not automatically an alert. Do not substitute an unsigned fake CRT to manufacture a runtime effect; inspect incidental startup alerts separately.

title: Potential Direct Syscall of NtOpenProcess
rationale: CallTrace starts UNKNOWN. Scientifically interesting but ordinary successful process access may not produce a C-reference alert. Inspect existing process-access captures as secondary evidence; do not introduce handcrafted syscall stubs to force qualification or label a C-negative case qualified.

title: Potential CommandLine Obfuscation Using Unicode Characters From Suspicious Image
rationale: Requires real listed shell identity and OriginalFileName as well as Unicode. A fixed shell child dominates the implementation; renaming the measured probe is not equivalent application behavior.

title: Potential Defense Evasion Via Right-to-Left Override
rationale: Same process/argument transport as proposed Unicode case. Actual U+202E is a valid predicate choice; literal escape/display strings also match but would weaken an encoding claim. Prefer one Unicode primary target.

title: Potential Defense Evasion Via Raw Disk Access By Uncommon Tools
rationale: Adds Event 9 and raw-volume I/O. Use only a harness-created disposable virtual disk/volume with known bytes; read and verify without writing during measurement. Confirm raw-device naming, permissions, event emission, and GUID attribution. Direct native APIs may limit runtime sensitivity; that is a limitation, not a reason to force a difference.

title: Sysmon File Executable Creation Detected
rationale: Event 29 rule is eligible but FileExecutableDetected is not configured explicitly in current sysmon.xml. Verify actual sensor enablement before admission; enabling it changes collection for all cases. Can initially evaluate existing benign PE creation fixtures rather than claim new behavior.

title: CreateRemoteThread API and LoadLibrary
rationale: Adds StartModule/StartFunction predicates beyond current target-image remote-thread rule. Consider only an owned disposable helper and benign fixed DLL. Higher implementation burden, source GUID attribution, export forwarding and actual reported module/function require qualification; do not force a specific alert by changing the rule or varying behavior by runtime.

title: Task Scheduler DLL Loaded By Application Located In Potentially Suspicious Location
rationale: Actual taskschd.dll load from a specified process location is feasible, but adds another DLL/path predicate rather than proving scheduled-task creation. Retain as an alternative only.

title: Signed DLL Loaded With Missing PE Version Metadata
rationale: Requires a valid non-Microsoft signature and wholly absent version metadata outside system paths. Certificate trust and crafted artifact metadata would dominate; limited incremental runtime value.

title: Potential CommandLine Obfuscation Using Unicode Characters
rationale: High relevance to runtime argument construction and encoding; Event 1 CommandLine contains one of the listed Unicode characters. Launch a fixed benign helper with identical Unicode argv and require exact argv receipt. Freeze wide-character semantics across languages; do not compare ANSI and Unicode APIs as if only runtime changed.

title: Suspicious Encoded Scripts in a WMI Consumer
rationale: Sigma Destination base64-offset predicate does not require RuleName, but a benign unbound consumer needs explicit object ownership, independent readback, cleanup, and new attribution logic. Meaningful future COM/WMI family; not ready under current harness.

title: Suspicious Scripting in a WMI Consumer
rationale: Sigma Destination script-string predicates. Benign inert/unbound content can test registration without executing a script; current process-only attribution is insufficient to assume ownership. Defer until a separate WMI contract exists.
